storage.title: Storing breast milk
storage.intro: Understand CDC guidance and how Milkee calculates storage deadlines.
sections: Freshly expressed milk

At 25 °C / 77 °F or below: up to 4 hours. In a refrigerator at 4 °C / 40 °F or below: up to 4 days. In a freezer at −18 °C / 0 °F or below: about 6 months is best; up to 12 months is acceptable. During travel, an insulated cooler with frozen ice packs can hold milk for up to 24 hours while keeping it cold.
Thawing and warming

CDC guidance allows 24 hours in the refrigerator from when milk is completely thawed, then 2 hours once warmed or brought to room temperature. Never refreeze thawed milk. Use bottle leftovers within 2 hours after the baby finishes feeding, then discard them. Do not microwave breast milk.
Milkee’s cautious choices

The app cannot know when thawing is complete. It therefore starts the 24-hour countdown when milk leaves the freezer and prevents refreezing. Moving cold milk to room-temperature storage starts a 2-hour limit. Any earlier, shorter deadline still applies. For reminders, one month means 30 days: freezer defaults to 180 days, with a maximum of 360 days.
Moving, merging and storage settings

A location’s name does not establish its temperature: set its physical conditions. Moving expired milk never makes it valid again. Merging keeps the earliest limit; cool fresh milk before combining it with cold milk. Shorter settings reduce deadlines; longer settings do not extend existing pouches. First freezing of still-valid fresh milk creates a freezer deadline, subject to inherited limits.
What the app cannot verify

Milkee tracks pouches, not bottle contact with a baby’s mouth: recording a used volume does not track bottle leftovers. You must check actual temperatures, hygiene, cold-chain interruptions and the accuracy of entries. Notifications depend on your phone and cannot guarantee an alert in time.
Your circumstances come first

This guidance concerns home storage for healthy, full-term infants. For premature, unwell or hospitalized babies, follow the care team’s instructions. The app never certifies that milk is safe. Ask a health professional when in doubt. Milkee is independent and is not endorsed or approved by the CDC. Original sources take precedence; this guide is an independent explanation.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What the website and app process, and the choices available to you.
sections: Contact and scope

Milkee is published by the GitHub account milkee-app. Use in-app support for requests about your personal data. The GitHub profile is the public contact; never post an email, account identifier, health information or login code in a public issue.
This website

Milkee adds no accounts, advertising, analytics or cookies to this website. Fonts and images are served with the site. GitHub Pages hosts the pages and may process technical connection data, including IP addresses, under its own policy. External links to Google Play, GitHub and the CDC are subject to those services’ policies.
App data

Account features use your email, an identifier, supplied profile details and sign-in provider. Milkee stores the volumes, dates, locations, operations, sharing and optional notes you enter to manage your stash. These records may reveal information about breastfeeding: keep notes to what is necessary. The app does not ask for a phone number. Supabase synchronizes account and stash data; a local cache helps the app operate.
Sharing and notifications

People you authorize can access stash information according to their permissions and shared locations. You can revoke access, but cannot remove copies they may already have kept. Notifications require system permission. Depending on configuration, support features process your messages, necessary technical details and a notification identifier for replies.
Optional analytics and support

PostHog analytics stay disabled until explicit consent for each account and device. With consent, your account identifier and email may be linked to a profile, and usage events, volumes, locations, screens and technical errors may be sent. These are not anonymous statistics. Secrets and free text are filtered. Withdrawing consent in Preferences stops future sending but does not erase data already received. Support may use PostHog Conversations independently of analytics consent: do not send passwords or unnecessary medical information.
Purposes, retention and providers

Accounts, synchronization and sharing provide the requested features; security and support operate the service and handle requests. Optional analytics rely on consent. Stash data remains linked to your account until you delete it or the account. Technical records, backups or support messages may persist under provider constraints; immediate erasure of all copies is not guaranteed. Supabase, PostHog, sign-in providers and GitHub are involved depending on the features used. Processing outside your country may occur; their policies and safeguards are linked below.
Your choices and rights

You can edit your data, revoke sharing, decline analytics and delete your account in the app. Use in-app support for access, correction, erasure or portability requests, handled under applicable rules. You may also contact your data protection authority, including the CNIL in France. Account deletion does not automatically remove historical PostHog data: request that erasure through support too. See Account deletion for steps.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: The essentials for using Milkee and understanding its limits.
sections: The service

Milkee organizes breast milk inventory: pouch entries, storage locations, indicative deadlines and sharing with authorized people. It does not diagnose conditions or replace advice from a health professional.
Account and sharing

Protect your sign-in methods, enter accurate information and share only with trusted people. You are responsible for the access you grant and must respect other users’ information. Do not bypass access controls or disrupt the service.
Storage and responsibility

Deadlines depend on your entries, selected conditions and available history. Milkee does not measure temperature or guarantee milk quality or safety. Read the storage guide and CDC sources; follow stricter instructions from your care team. An absent or late reminder is never proof of safety.
Availability and changes

Access depends on your device, network and third-party services. Interruptions and synchronization errors can occur. Check information before relying on it for care. Features and these texts may change; each page shows its update date.
Leaving and your rights

You can stop using Milkee and delete your account in account details. Mandatory legal rights, including consumer and data protection rights, remain applicable; these terms do not exclude them. Brands, content and software remain subject to their owners’ rights. For help, use in-app support or the public GitHub profile without disclosing personal data.

legal.title: Legal information
legal.intro: Publisher, hosting and references for the Milkee website.
sections: Publisher and public contact
The Milkee website and app are published by the GitHub account milkee-app. The profile linked below is the public contact. Use in-app support for private requests concerning your account.
Hosting

This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. Official hosting information and contact details are available through the links below. This website does not receive your stash records.
References and independence

Milk storage guidance links to original publications from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Milkee is not affiliated with the CDC or Google. Translations and explanations here are provided by Milkee and are not official CDC translations. Google Play and other cited brands belong to their respective owners.
Health information

Content is for information and organization. It is not personalized medical advice, a health certification or a guarantee of milk safety. Ask a health professional about individual circumstances. Sources were consulted on November 25, 2026.

support.title: Help and frequently asked questions
support.intro: Get started and find the right support.
sections: How do I start?

Install Milkee from Google Play, create an account and check the physical storage conditions for your locations. Add pouches using their real pumping dates and volumes. Website screenshots use demonstration data and may differ from your version.
How do I share my stash?
Open relationships in the app, invite a trusted person and choose permissions and accessible locations. Review the access you grant and revoke it when no longer needed.
Why am I not receiving reminders?

Check Milkee Preferences and the notification permission in your phone settings. Battery restrictions and the operating system may delay reminders. Check your inventory regularly; alerts are not guaranteed.
Is my data public?
Your stash is not published on this website. App access follows your account and sharing permissions. Analytics are optional; support is available without accepting them.
Report a problem

Use in-app support first for account-related requests. For a public, non-sensitive issue, you can open an issue in the website repository. Describe the app version and problem without emails, stash data, identifiers or login codes.
What about iPhone?
The verified download link currently published here is for Google Play. No App Store link is announced until a public listing is verified.

delete-account.title: Account deletion
delete-account.intro: You stay in control of your Milkee account.
sections: In the app
Open your profile, then account details. Choose Delete account and accept both confirmation prompts. This action is irreversible. Uninstalling the app does not delete your account.
Data covered

Deletion initiates removal of the account and linked service data, including the profile, pouches and sharing relationships. Sign-out clears the session and local cache. Copies kept by people you shared with cannot be removed from their devices.
Analytics, support and backups

Account deletion does not automatically erase events already received by PostHog or support conversations. Request their erasure through in-app support before deleting your account. Backup constraints and applicable obligations may delay deletion of some technical copies; no single deletion period is stated.
If you cannot access the app

You can try account recovery from the sign-in screen. This website currently provides no form or private channel for requesting deletion without the app. The GitHub profile is for public technical questions and does not provide private messaging: never post your email, personal data, password or access codes there.
